**Affected part:** Ear (kernels on the cob)

**Key visual features:**
- Yellow/orange kernels covered with dark green to blue-green mold growth
- Mold appears between and on kernel surfaces, giving a mottled green-black appearance
- The coloration (teal/dark green) is characteristic of *Trichoderma* species, which produce distinctive green spore masses
- Husks are dry/brown, ear is partially exposed
- No pink/red (rules out Gibberella), no gray-white mycelium (rules out Diplodia), no black aspergillus (rules out Aspergillus)

The dark green to teal mold on kernels is the hallmark of *Trichoderma* ear rot, caused by *Trichoderma* spp. which produce characteristic green conidia.
